# Desktop Hand

**Real desktop mouse/keyboard control for DeepSeek Harness, plus a policy-guarded file
toolkit with

quarantined deletion, session authorization, an emergency-stop hotkey and an
append-only audit log.*

uarantined deletion, session authorization, an emergency-stop hotkey and an
append-only audit log.**

> ## ⚠️ HIGH RISK — READ THIS FIRST
>
> Desktop Hand lets the model **operate your physical desktop*

*: move the real mouse pointer,
> click, drag, type, press shortcuts, take screenshots — and write,

move, delete and restore
> **real files** on your machine.
>
> - Real input and file mutations are *

*OFF by default**. They require an explicit,
>   **session-scoped, time- and action-budgeted** grant

that a human approves (default
>   `approval.authorize: "ask"`; if your DSH approval policy auto-ap

proves prompts, that
>   safeguard is weakened — see docs/CONFIG.md).
> - This is **not a sandbox**.

It is not a VM, not a separate user account, and not an OS
>   permission boundary. Desktop Hand ru

ns with the same privileges as DeepSeek Harness and
>   can touch anything that process can touch, e

xcept for the paths protected by policy.
> - The filesystem policy governs **Desktop Hand tools only

** (unless you opt in to
>   `policy.enforceOnDshFsTools`). Shell tools (`bash`, `pwsh`, …) are not

governed and can
>   bypass it.
> - Deletion defaults to **trash/quarantine mode** (recoverable), bu

t `direct` mode is
>   permanently destructive when a user unlocks it.
> - **Start with the fake pro

vider or a throwaway test account, walk through
>   docs/ACCEPTANCE.md, and keep a hand on the emerg

ency-stop hotkey.**
>   The default hotkey is **Pause** (deliberately not `F9`: Blender uses `F9` fo

r *Adjust Last
>   Operation*, so F9 would fire while modelling).

## What it is

Desktop Hand is a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that gives the model two carefully separated
capabil

p Hand is a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that gives the model two carefully separated
capabilities:

1. **Real desktop input** — observe the screen (`get_pointer`, `foreground_window`,
`screenshot`) an

d act on the physical desktop (`move_mouse`, `click`, `drag`, `scroll`,
`press_key`, `type_text`). T

he model works in a *see → act → see* loop: screenshot, view it
with DSH's `read_image`, perform **o

ne** action, screenshot again.
2. **Policy-guarded file operations** — `read_file`, `list_dir`, `wri

te_file`, `move_path`,
`delete_path`, `restore_path`, `list_trash`. Reads are unprivileged but still

subject to
protected zones; writes/moves/deletes need a separate **files** grant. Deletion defaults

## Requirements and platform support
| Platform | Real input | Screenshots | Emergency hotkey | Notes |
| **Windows 10/11** | ✅ full | ✅ full | ✅ default **Pause** | Primary target. Uses Windows PowerShel
l 5.1 (`powershell.exe`) with `pwsh.exe` as fallback, a persistent agent and a hidden hotkey monitor

. No extra installs required. |
| **Linux** | ⚠️ best effort | ⚠️ best effort | ❌ none | Requires `x
dotool` on PATH; screenshots need ImageMagick `import`, `scrot` or `gnome-screenshot`. Multi-monitor
geometry is reported as one display. Emergency stop still works via `/desktop-hand stop` / `desktop

_hand_emergency_stop`; the provider also checks the stop-flag file. |
| **macOS** | ⚠️ best effort |
⚠️ best effort | ❌ none | Requires `cliclick`; uses `osascript`, `pbcopy`+`Cmd+V` for typing (this
**changes the clipboard**) and `screencapture`. Scrolling and middle-click are unsupported; drag is
left-button only; Accessibility/Automation permissions must be granted manually. No hotkey monitor.

|
| **fake** | — (simulated) | ✅ writes a real PNG | ❌ none | Deterministic in-memory provider for t

ests/dry runs (`input.provider: "fake"`). Never touches the real desktop. |
| **disabled** | ❌ | ❌ |
❌ | `input.provider: "disabled"`; input tools fail closed. |

Runtime requirements: **Node.js ≥ 22** (the plugin is ESM; `package.json` `engines`), DSH with a
pro

file, and for Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7. The test suite in this repo was run on
Node **
v26.13.0** on Windows.
## Security model and threat model
### Threat model and honest limitations

Desktop Hand assumes the **human user is the principal** and the model may be wrong, manipulated
by
prompt injection, or simply confused:

- A compromise is contained by the grant's time/action budget, the emergency hotkey, the trash's
rec

overability and the audit trail — **not** by an OS sandbox.
- **Policy scope:** `policy.*` governs *

*Desktop Hand's own tools only**. Unless you set
`policy.enforceOnDshFsTools: true` (which also guar

ds DSH's `read`/`read_image`/`list_dir`/
`write`/`edit`/`write_file`), a shell command (`bash`, `pws

h`, …) can read or modify the same
files, including paths inside read-only zones, and **bypasses the

delete modes entirely**.
A `forbid` mode is not a filesystem permission.
- **Not an OS sandbox.** T

he plugin runs with the DSH process's user privileges. It cannot
protect you from a malicious proces

s running as the same user, nor from the model being
socially engineered into obtaining a broad gran

t.
- **Screen privacy:** screenshots capture everything visible on all monitors (or the requested
re

gion). `type_text` can type secrets. Text is redacted in the audit by default
(`audit.logTypedText:

false`) but is still sent as real input.
- **Destructive paths remain:** a human who unlocks `direct

-delete`, supplies `confirm_direct`
and approves can permanently delete files; `trashDir` contents a

re not auto-purged but can be
deleted manually outside the plugin, and the plugin cannot protect the

m if you configure the
trash on an untrusted/unprotected volume.
- **Approval dependency:** `approva

l.fileMutations`, `approval.directDelete`, `approval.drag` and
`approval.combo` default to `ask`; de

ployments without a live approval channel (e.g. DSH
approval policy `never`, headless runs) will rej

ect those operations. This is deliberate
fail-closed behavior, not a bug.
- **Platform gaps:** the e

mergency hotkey monitor is **Windows-only**; on Linux/macOS the
`/desktop-hand stop` command and the

stop-flag checks are the emergency path. The Linux/macOS
providers are best-effort, and macOS typin

g changes the clipboard.
